rules.evidence: The target owns informational review and risk-evaluation intent. The protected /baths page owns project/order intent; the article links to it without presenting it as an Evtenia modular-bath offer.
The lead directly explains what makes owner reviews useful: identifiable construction, use, scope, delivery and installation context.
The article covers review signals, conditional benefits, risks, a pre-contract checklist, fit and FAQs. It adds a comparison checklist rather than repeating generic promotional claims.

The live /baths catalog was checked on 2026-10-09. It labels listed projects as frame, timber and log construction, not modular; the article states this plainly and invents no Evtenia cases or customer reviews.

Fire-safety context links to current MChS guidance checked on 2026-10-09. The article gives no installation clearances or DIY stove instructions and directs readers to equipment documentation and a qualified installer.
No claimed survey of reviews, universal prices, schedules, warranties, heat-up times, service life or quantified performance. Advantages and downsides are expressed conditionally.
Includes contextual links to /baths (required commercial owner), /services/fundament and /contacts.
Oleg Ivanovich Kislyakov is the technical author/reviewer. The site owner previously approved review attribution for him on technical articles.

Unique Latin slug, title, excerpt, category, author, reviewer and 137-character SEO description are set. Existing production robots.txt allows public pages and names the sitemap; the backend emits self-canonical article pages and includes published articles in sitemap.xml.
1,268 body words; no H1 inside content, placeholders, scripts, iframes, inline handlers or javascript URLs. Frontend sanitizer preserves the used semantic elements and journal classes.
The new slug is registered in managed production sync and gets a dedicated Journal category idempotently. Production URL and sitemap entry are to be verified immediately after deployment.
